newsitem.title: USA: U.S. appeals court blocks California execution.
newsitem.headline: U.S. appeals court blocks California execution.

text.p: A federal appeals court Sunday threw out the death sentence of a man convicted of a 1981 rape and murder less than 48 hours before he was due to be executed.
In an unusual decision, an 11-judge panel of the 9th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeal voted 7-4 to annul Thomas Thompson's death sentence and ordered that he receive a new trial on the rape conviction.

Thompson, 42, had been scheduled to die by lethal injection at San Quentin State Prison near San Francisco soon after midnight Monday for the 1981 rape and murder of Ginger Fleischli, 20, in Laguna Beach, southern California.

The appeals court panel said in a written ruling that it was throwing out the death sentence and ordering a new trial on Thompson's rape conviction. Rape was a "special circumstance" which made Thompson eligible for the death penalty under California law.

The panel agreed with a district court judge who found in 1995 that Thompson's trial attorney "provided constitutionally deficient representation in failing to refute the rape evidence and in failing to impeach the testimony of a notoriously unreliable jailhouse informant."

The district court had earlier been overruled by a smaller panel of the appeals court which had reinstated Thompson's death sentence. The latest decision blocks Thompson's execution although the state is expected to appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court to overturn the decision.
